title: New Zealand Recall Allen, Ferguson and Seifert for India ODI Series
excerpt: Finn Allen and Lockie Ferguson return to the 50-over setup for the first time since 2023, joining the final two ODIs as New Zealand test their depth a year out from the World Cup.
body:
• Finn Allen and Lockie Ferguson return to the ODI setup after last playing the format in 2023; Tim Seifert's last ODI was 18 months ago against Pakistan.
  • The trio joins for the final two ODIs (Nov 12 and Nov 15) as seven players rotate in and Test-bound players head to Wellington early.
  • Rachin Ravindra returns from a shoulder injury for the first three ODIs; Mitchell Santner captains both squads.
  • The series is New Zealand's key build-up window with the ODI World Cup one year away — a deliberate squad-depth experiment.

New Zealand have recalled explosive batter Finn Allen, fast bowler Lockie Ferguson and wicketkeeper-batter Tim Seifert for the final two matches of their five-game ODI series against India, New Zealand Cricket (NZC) announced on Sunday. The series begins on November 4 at Eden Park in Auckland and runs through November 15.

The recall marks a genuine comeback for all three. Allen and Ferguson last played a 50-over international in 2023 — Ferguson's most recent outing came in the World Cup semi-final against India in Mumbai — while Seifert has not featured in the format for 18 months, since a home series against Pakistan. All three will join the squad for the fourth and fifth ODIs, replacing a group of players who will depart after the third match in Hamilton on November 10 to begin Test preparations.

Two squads, one plan

New Zealand have effectively named two different squads for the series, a split driven by the quick turnaround into the Test leg. Mitchell Santner will captain both groups. The red-ball core — Conway, Henry, Jamieson, Latham, Mitchell, Phillips, Ravindra and Nathan Smith — features only in the first three ODIs before heading to Wellington for the first Test, beginning November 19.

In their place for the final two games come Allen, Ferguson, Seifert, Kristian Clarke, Matt Fisher, Mitch Hay and Nick Kelly, giving 21 players involvement across the series. It is a deliberate rotation policy, and head coach Rob Walter framed it as a long-term investment rather than mere workload management.

"With the ODI World Cup just one year away it's important for us to also view these matches as valuable preparation for that event. Bringing in seven players for the final ODIs allows us to test our depth and see how those players fare against a world-class side."

— Rob Walter, New Zealand head coach

Walter was direct about what the three recalled players bring. "We're incredibly lucky to have the depth that we do to have 21 players involved in the series," he said in a statement. "It's also great to bring guys like Lockie, Finn, and Tim back into the one day unit. They're all exciting and explosive players in their own right and are proven match winners." He added that for Allen and Seifert in particular, the series is "a great opportunity for them to push their case in the longer format" after establishing themselves as T20 specialists.

Context & Background

The recall comes with New Zealand in rare ascendancy in this fixture. In January, the Black Caps secured a historic 2-1 ODI series win in India — their first bilateral ODI series victory over India on Indian soil — and now host the return leg riding that momentum. The core of that squad has been retained, with Ravindra the notable returnee: he dislocated his shoulder during a promotional shoot last month and was ruled out of the T20I series beginning October 22, but has recovered in time for the opening three ODIs.

Injuries forced the selectors' hand: Zak Foulkes (hip flexor), Will O'Rourke (calf) and Ben Sears (ankle) were all unavailable, clearing the path for Ferguson's return with his raw pace.

Impact & Analysis

For India, the two-squad announcement is genuinely useful intelligence. The visitors face a settled, full-strength New Zealand in the first three matches and a rotated, fresher — if less proven — lineup for the final two. Ferguson's return is the sharpest tactical concern: his 150-kph pace is the kind of threat India have not faced in this format since 2023.

The bigger signal is strategic. With the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia a year out, New Zealand are using a home series against top-tier opposition as a live audition — seven new faces against India is a high-pressure test of depth, and Walter's comments make it explicit that selection for the World Cup will be informed by these games.

Diaspora Angle

The series is a major draw for the large Indian diaspora in New Zealand, where Eden Park and Hamilton crowds routinely carry strong Indian support — the Auckland fixture on November 4 is expected to play in front of a packed, divided house, much like the T20I series preceding it. For Indian-origin fans, the squad announcement also doubles as a scouting report: the New Zealand lineup India faces in the final two ODIs will look materially different from the one in the first three.

What's Next

The five-match T20I series runs October 22 to November 1 before the ODIs begin. New Zealand will announce their 14-player Test squad in early November, with the World Test Championship series at Wellington (from November 19) carrying championship points that matter. Watch whether Allen, Ferguson and Seifert force their way into long-term contention — the next ODI assignment, and the 2027 World Cup squad, will be decided on the back of how they handle these two games.
